fields.label: Intro
paragraphs: Most of what we already supply is bonded. These six are the families where the metal and the rubber have to work as one component, and where a bond that separates is a failure of the whole assembly rather than a cosmetic defect.
marked: Most of what we already supply is bonded. These six are the families where the metal and the rubber have to work as one component, and where a bond that separates is a failure of the whole assembly rather than a cosmetic defect.
fields.note: 42 words · “most of what we already supply is bonded” is the honest framing and it is the argument for this page existing at all

fields.label: Cards ×6
rows: Sandwich, bobbin and conical mounts with rubber vulcanised between two metal faces. The bond carries every load the mount carries, in shear and in compression, for the life of the machine.
Inner sleeve, rubber, outer sleeve, bonded in one cure. Torsional stiffness comes from the rubber section and the interference; the bond is what stops the sleeve spinning inside the housing.
A rubber covering bonded to a steel or aluminium core, ground to your outside diameter and concentricity after cure. Bonded rather than sleeved, so it cannot creep under torque.
A rubber sealing element moulded onto a metal stem. The rubber does the sealing and the metal takes the drive load, and nothing between them is an adhesive joint added later.
Where a diaphragm drives a stem or seats against a plate, the metal is bonded in during cure — no assembly stack, no adhesive line, no tolerance chain between two parts.
Sheet rubber bonded to a steel vessel, sump or chute to protect it from abrasion or chemical attack. Same process, larger scale, and bonded rather than mechanically fixed.

sections.title: How the bond is made
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → accordion, three panels, from the /products/bellows material accordion

fields.label: H2
lines: Three Steps, and the Third Is the Cure
fields.value: Three Steps, and the Third Is the Cure
fields.note: 8 words · the heading carries the argument. The bond is not a fourth step added after moulding — it happens during it, and that is the whole distinction

fields.label: Panel 1 — Metal preparation
paragraphs: Every bond failure we have ever seen started here. The metal is degreased, grit-blasted to a controlled profile and chemically treated, then bonded within a defined window before the surface re-oxidises. A part that sits overnight between blasting and priming is a part that will delaminate in service, so preparation and priming run as one operation, not two shifts.
marked: Every bond failure we have ever seen started here. The metal is degreased, grit-blasted to a controlled profile and chemically treated, then bonded within a defined window before the surface re-oxidises. A part that sits overnight between blasting and priming is a part that will delaminate in service, so preparation and priming run as one operation, not two shifts.
fields.note: 60 words · the most persuasive paragraph on the page and it costs nothing to state. Every experienced buyer knows surface preparation is where bonds are won and lost; saying it first, and naming the failure mode we design against, reads as a supplier who has debugged this rather than one who has read about it

fields.label: Panel 2 — Two-coat bonding system
paragraphs: A primer goes onto the prepared metal and a cover coat over it, matched to the compound being bonded. The primer grips the metal; the cover coat co-vulcanises with the rubber. The two are a system — a cover coat chosen for natural rubber will not hold FKM — so the bonding system is selected with the compound, not after it.
marked: A primer goes onto the prepared metal and a cover coat over it, matched to the compound being bonded. The primer grips the metal; the cover coat co-vulcanises with the rubber. The two are a system — a cover coat chosen for natural rubber will not hold FKM — so the bonding system is selected with the compound, not after it.
fields.note: 58 words · describes the standard two-coat architecture without naming a brand. No adhesive supplier is named, which keeps the page accurate whichever system a given part uses and avoids implying an approval Margo does not hold

fields.label: Panel 3 — Bonded during vulcanisation
paragraphs: The prepared insert is loaded into the tool and the rubber is moulded onto it. Heat and pressure cure the compound and complete the bond in the same cycle, so the finished part comes out of the tool as one component. Nothing is glued, clamped or pressed together afterwards, and there is no assembly joint to inspect, because there is no assembly.

fields.note: 61 words · the payoff for the two panels above. This is the sentence that should be quoted back to us in an enquiry, and it is written to be extractable on its own

fields.label: Closing note
paragraphs: Tooling is cut in-house, so the insert location, the flash line and the bond area are designed together rather than negotiated between a toolroom and a moulder. First samples come back 48 to 72 hours from an approved drawing.

sections.title: How the bond is verified
sections.chip: New · carries the page’s one CONFIRM
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → quality block, from the /products/gaskets component

fields.label: H2
lines: A Good Bond Fails in the Rubber
fields.value: A Good Bond Fails in the Rubber
fields.note: 7 words · the best heading in this content set. It states the industry’s actual acceptance criterion, it is checkable, it is true, and it replaces the bond-strength number this page is not allowed to publish with something more rigorous than a number would have been

fields.label: Body
paragraphs: Bond quality is judged by where the part breaks, not by how hard it was to break. Pull a sound bonded component apart and the tear runs through the rubber, leaving a rubber-covered metal face; a poor bond separates cleanly at the interface and the metal comes back bare. ASTM D429 puts a notation on that — R for failure in the rubber, RC at the rubber-to-cover-coat line, CP between cover coat and primer, M at the metal. The target is 100% R, and anything else is a rejected process, not a weaker part.
leads: ASTM D429 puts a notation on that
marked: Bond quality is judged by where the part breaks, not by how hard it was to break. Pull a sound bonded component apart and the tear runs through the rubber, leaving a rubber-covered metal face; a poor bond separates cleanly at the interface and the metal comes back bare. **ASTM D429 puts a notation on that** — **R** for failure in the rubber, **RC** at the rubber-to-cover-coat line, **CP** between cover coat and primer, **M** at the metal. **The target is 100% R, and anything else is a rejected process, not a weaker part.**
fields.note: 98 words · this is the page. It gives a specifier something to write into a drawing note, it is the real language of bonded-part qualification, and it lets Margo make a rigorous claim without publishing a single number. Competitor pages in this category publish a peel strength and nothing else — a figure from a specimen that says nothing about their part

fields.label: Test table
rows: ASTM D429 · failure mode to 100% R
Sample per batch, NABL partner laboratory
fields.note:
ANSWERED 2026-09-03 — destructive adhesion testing runs at the NABL partner laboratory.
Client-confirmed: at the NABL partner laboratory. The row now reads “sample per batch, NABL partner laboratory”, which puts D429 on the same footing as tear, fluid immersion and ozone — tested, and tested somewhere nameable.
Margo’s published test list — hardness, tensile, compression set, ozone, fluid immersion, brittleness, abrasion, tear, rebound, flammability — does not include D429. Every moulder doing bonded work destroys a sample per batch and reads the failure mode; that is ordinary practice, not a capability claim. The row now says where it happens. That matters more than the method name: a buyer qualifying a bonded-part supplier checks whether the adhesion test is real or asserted, and a named laboratory is the difference.
The struck row stays struck. Dynamic fatigue is not held anywhere, exactly as on the bellows and diaphragms pages, and a bonded mount is precisely the part a buyer will ask cycle life about

sections.title: Technical & commercial questions
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → FAQ accordion, six questions, from the /products/bellows component · these six are the FAQPage mainEntity, verbatim

fields.label: Q1

lines: Can you bond rubber to aluminium and stainless steel?

parts.text: Yes to both, with the right preparation and primer. Aluminium needs an etch or conversion coat and stainless needs a different primer from mild steel, so tell us the alloy or the grade with the drawing. The two things that will stop us are anodising and plating — bond to the bare substrate and finish the exposed metal afterwards, or supply the insert unplated.

fields.note: 64 words · the highest-volume qualifying question in this category, answered yes with the condition attached rather than yes with a caveat buried in a datasheet

fields.label: Q2

parts.text: We do not publish a peel or tensile figure, because a number from a test specimen tells you nothing about your part — bond strength scales with area, geometry and compound, and a headline figure is read as a guarantee for parts it was never measured on. The criterion we work to is the failure mode. A sound bond tears through the rubber and leaves the metal covered; a poor one separates clean and leaves it bare. ASTM D429 calls the first 100% R, and that is what we qualify to on your part, on your insert, with the report in your name.
parts.lead: The criterion we work to is the failure mode.

fields.note: 104 words · the most important answer on the page and the direct counterpart to the diaphragms page refusing cycle life. Refusing the number and offering the criterion is a stronger commercial position, because the number would be read as a warranty and the criterion is read as competence

fields.label: Q3

lines: Do you bond during moulding or glue the parts afterwards?

parts.text: During moulding, always. The prepared and primed insert goes into the tool and the rubber is moulded onto it, so heat and pressure cure the compound and complete the bond in the same cycle. The part leaves the tool as one component. Nothing is glued, clamped or pressed together afterwards — there is no assembly joint, because there is no assembly.

fields.note: 61 words · the question a buyer asks when a previous supplier’s part delaminated. Answering it as a flat process fact, not a selling point, is what makes it land

fields.label: Q4

lines: Can you supply the metal inserts, or do we send them?

parts.text: Either. Send your inserts and we bond to them, or send the drawing and we source and prepare them here. Sourcing them here is usually the better route on a new part, because insert design, tool design and bond area are one decision rather than three, and our toolroom is in the same building.

fields.note: 55 words · a commercial question with a technical answer, and it surfaces the in-house toolroom for the second time without repeating the earlier sentence

fields.label: Q5

lines: What is the minimum order quantity for bonded components?

parts.text: We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or quoted against the part where geometry or tooling makes that unrealistic. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum. On a bonded part with a bought-in insert the insert lead time usually sets the schedule rather than the moulding, so tell us your call-off pattern with the volume.

fields.note: 64 words · the standard answer, client-instructed 2026-09-01, with one part-specific sentence appended — the same pattern the SKU sheets use. The standard sentences are not reworded

fields.label: Q6

lines: What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?

parts.text: TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment. Production is three to four weeks from drawing approval, or two weeks on an express basis where we have confirmed capacity.

fields.note: 48 words · the standard commercial string, unchanged, with the sitewide 3–4 week lead time
